messages:
maria: Heads up — getting a spike of apiserver 5xx in eastus-1 around 08:12 UTC, correlated with large NVLink attach churn from a GPU fleet scale. etcd leader latency briefly >200ms and controller-manager started restarting a few pods. can someone @oncall take a look?

jason: I'm on it. grabbing metrics now. seeing KV write latency and a burst of attach events to the gpu-pool autoscaler.

liam: logs from the provisioner show lots of failed attach attempts: `AttachVolume timeout` interleaved with `nvlink: peer attach race`

maria: rough command outputs: 
``` 
# kubectl -n kube-system get pods | egrep "apiserver|etcd|controller-manager"
apiserver-eastus-1   3/3   Running   0   20m
etcd-eastus-1        3/3   Running   0   42m
controller-manager-1 0/1   CrashLoopBackOff  4   18m
```

srinivas: controller-manager logs show leader election timeouts: `Failed to renew lease: context deadline exceeded` — looks like apiserver was slow to respond to leader heartbeats.

maria: potential chain: NVLink attach surge -> kernel attach ops saturate host IO -> apiserver latency (due to kubelet/volume calls) -> controller-manager lease renewal fails -> restarts.

jason: I pushed a quick mitigation: scaled down noncritical GPU attach jobs in eastus job-queue and raised attach timeout on provisioner from 10s -> 30s. monitoring now.

deploy-bot: rollback window started for gpu-provisioner v2.3.1 -> v2.2.9 in eastus at 08:26 UTC as requested by jason.

liam: after scale-down, etcd p99 latency dropped from 210ms -> 45ms within ~3 minutes. apiserver 5xx rate decreased. controller-manager pods recovered one-by-one.

maria: good. can we get root cause? is this a race in nvlink attach path or a host kernel bug? need a postmortem and a short-term guard.

srinivas: attaching traces from node-level: high /sysfs contention during NVLink peer negotiation. I suspect driver + kernel backpressure. filing issue with infra-driver team.

jason: short-term guard ideas: limit concurrent attach requests per node, throttle autoscaler bursts, and add a fast-fail fallback in provisioner to retry on a staggered schedule. also consider isolating attach-intensive jobs to specific nodepools (no controlplane-hosts).

maria: agree. add ticket to backlog — tag as P2 but include cost/regulatory note because Dedicated customers could hit this. callout: we must avoid global apiserver SLO regressions during GPU onboarding.

liam: note on costs: throttling autoscaler increases ephemeral CPU-backed fallback usage which could spike short-term bill by ~3-5% in eastus. will include numbers in the ticket.

jason: monitoring updates: added a dashboard tile for `nvlink_attach_rate`, `attach_fail_rate`, `etcd_p99` and a runbook link. also added alert: etdc_p99>150ms for >2m AND attach_fail_rate>5% -> pager.

maria: nice. can someone schedule a quick sync with driver infra team and node-ops tomorrow 09:00 UTC? I want an action owner for the driver bug, autoscaler backoff, and the provisioner retry pattern.

srinivas: I'll own driver bug triage. created ticket RH-INFRA-4362 with logs.

jason: I'll own autoscaler change and the alerting.

maria: thanks all. leaving this thread open for followups. :thumbsup:
